text:
Registered residential sales reached 11,041 units valued at AED 32,077,251,613 in the last four weeks, representing a 9.2 percent increase in volume and a 16.5 percent rise in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,312, which are recorded separately from sales. The off-plan segment accounted for 58.7 percent of all transactions during this timeframe.

The median residential price per square foot stood at AED 1,672, marking a 1.3 percent decline from the previous four-week median of AED 1,694. Top performing areas by sales volume included Dubai South with 3,836 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,252 units over the last twelve weeks. Business Bay recorded a median of AED 2,121 per square foot, while Majan showed a 1.8 percent price increase over the same twelve-week window.

Rental activity remained robust with 93,471 Ejari contracts registered, where renewals constituted 50.3 percent of the total. The median annual residential rent was AED 70,000. Estimated gross yields were highest in Zaabeel First at 9.0 percent for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent and Town Square at 7.0 percent. Dubai South offered an estimated yield of 4.6 percent despite leading in sales volume.

Market dynamics show distinct divergence across communities. Al Yufrah 1 heated up with a 41.7 percent price increase, while Palm Jumeirah cooled by 18.4 percent over twelve weeks. Al Hebiah First saw an 11.1 percent decline with 100 percent of its benchmark sales being off-plan. The anomaly monitor flagged 972 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. Figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals and outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
